how: Singapore Ballet runs term-based adult beginner classes (no prior experience needed).
Many studios offer cheap trial classes in salsa, bachata and kizomba; no partner needed.
Los Tarantos (Singapore Flamenco Club, NAFA) and Spanish Dance Singapore teach flamenco at all levels.
SIFAS and Apsaras Arts teach this Indian classical dance from beginner to advanced; LASALLE ran an adult short course.
Clan and athletic associations run lion dance troupes with beginner training in drumming and footwork; Chinatown has run public workshops.
venue: Chin Woo Athletic Association lion dance troupe

how: SIFAS teaches Kathak; Apsaras Arts has also run Kathak classes.
SwingStation teaches Lindy Hop levels 1-3 at Aliwal Arts Centre; Jitterbugs Swingapore also offers it.
EV Dance and Kulture Studios run hip-hop and b-boy classes; SCAPE has hosted breaking intensives.
A weekly beginner Argentine tango group class runs on Wednesdays at Allenby House; no partner needed.
Irish Inspirational Dance is a Singapore school with an adult class, listed by the Irish Embassy.
Sri Warisan Som Said runs public Malay dance workshops (inang, asli, zapin, joget), e.g. at the Singapore Heritage Festival; regular classes unverified.
venue: Sri Warisan Som Said Performing Arts

how: Several dedicated studios (The Brass Barre, SLAP, PXD) offer pole classes with cheap trials.
Adult beginner tap classes are listed in Bugis, and Tanglin Arts Studio teaches tap among other genres.
Circus Swingapore and Aerial Fitness Studio teach silks, lyra and static trapeze to beginners.
Dozens of private studios and music schools teach adult piano.
Many music schools and private teachers offer guitar lessons.
Eason Music School and other Chinese music schools offer guzheng group and private lessons.
Eason Music School teaches erhu privately; People's Association community centres run 10-session adult erhu courses that can lead into community Chinese orchestras.
venue: People's Association community centre courses (ONE PA)

how: SIFAS is cited by NLB as offering sitar lessons; current class status not confirmed.
SIFAS has a resident tabla guru (Supriyo Banerjee); enrolment requires SIFAS membership.
Gamelan is mostly played in school/polytechnic CCAs; NUS Singa Nglaras Gamelan Ensemble also accepts outside members.
Pipe bands exist in schools (ACS Independent Boys' Brigade, Northland Secondary) and the Women Police Pipes and Drums Band; public lessons not confirmed.
Rave Harps Academy and private teachers (listed on harpcenter) teach harp; NAFA and NUS YST Conservatory have harp programmes.
Only one-off past events (a 2018 NUS master class, a 2019 YST forum) were found; no regular theremin lessons located.
HIBIKIYA and Mangrove Learning (formerly School of Daiko) teach taiko, including adult courses via ONE PA.
Non-auditioned adult choirs such as VOS Chorus of the People and Vox Camerata welcome beginners.
Volunteer orchestras like Braddell Heights Symphony Orchestra, Orchestra of the Music Makers and The Philharmonic Orchestra recruit amateur players.
Community Chinese orchestras (e.g. Keat Hong Chinese Orchestra) run under community clubs, and ONE PA erhu courses feed into them.
The Improv Company, founded 2013, is Singapore's improv school and runs beginner courses.
Weekly open mics (Talk Cock Comedy at Blu Jaz Cafe) and short beginner courses like Grab the Mic let novices perform.
venue: Blu Jaz Cafe (Talk Cock Comedy open mic)

how: Republic Polytechnic's magic group runs workshops for amateurs; IBM Singapore Ring 115 is the local society; adult classes were not confirmed.
Zouk Academy, E-TracX DJ Skool and Show Ning DJ School teach DJing on Pioneer decks; equipment can be rented.
Ableton Certified Trainers (Ben Ang, Syafiq Halid) and Garnish Music Production teach production; NUS Electronic Music Lab also exists.
Singapore Teochew Poit Ip Huay Kuan ran 10-week Teochew opera singing classes; Nam Hwa Opera trains children and adults.
venue: Singapore Teochew Poit Ip Huay Kuan

how: Time Out lists several acting classes and workshops for adults in Singapore.
No known tradition, teacher or group in Singapore was found (not searched in depth).
No alphorn teaching or ensemble found; the instrument is tied to alpine regions and no local group is known (not searched).
No Morris side is known in Singapore (not searched in depth).
No kabuki troupe or school exists in Singapore; training is in Japan.
